excerpt_i18n.en: According to Leifeng Network, the 8th GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced on December 12-13, 2025, at the Sheraton Shenzhen Bo'lin Tianrui Hotel. As a benchmark event in the AI industry-academia-research-investment community, GAIR has consistently adhered to the core principle of "heritage + innovation" since its inception in 2016, dedicated to bridging cutting-edge technology with industrial practice. As artificial intelligence increasingly becomes a core variable in national competition, computing power is reshaping technological pathways and industrial structures at an unprecedented pace. The "AI Computing Power in the Next Decade" session held on the 13th focused on computing power—the foundational core of intelligent systems—engaging in systematic discussions from architectural evolution and ecosystem development to industrial implementation, aiming to clarify key variables and development directions for China's AI industry over the next ten years. Addressing the opportunities and challenges in domestic computing power infrastructure and large-scale model development, Professor Liu Fangming delivered a keynote speech titled "Systemic Challenges of Domestic Computing Power-Driven Large Models: Full-Lifecycle Toolchains and Demonstration Applications." As AI computing power competition enters a "deep-water zone," national laboratories are becoming the "ballast" for domestically controlled, self-reliant systems, developing "super-intelligent data-integrated architecture" computing clusters and fully localized model toolchains. Professor Liu Fangming noted that "national team" institutions, represented by research bodies like Peng Cheng Laboratory, have the core mission of securing the baseline for domestic AI self-reliance—avoiding competition with enterprises for profit or with universities for prestige, and focusing on the "hard and heavy tasks" within the domestic ecosystem that are "unable, unwilling, or hesitant to be undertaken," ensuring the realization of computing capabilities even without reliance on overseas hardware.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según informa Leifeng, los días 12 y 13 de diciembre de 2025, se inauguró oficialmente la octava edición de la Conferencia Global de Inteligencia Artificial y Robótica (GAIR) en el Sheraton Shenzhen Boao Tianrui Hotel. Como evento de referencia en el ámbito de la investigación, educación, industria e inversión en IA, GAIR, desde su creación en 2016, ha mantenido el núcleo de "herencia + innovación" y se ha dedicado a conectar la vanguardia tecnológica con la práctica industrial. En un momento en que la inteligencia artificial se está convirtiendo gradualmente en una variable central en la competencia entre naciones, la potencia de cálculo está remodelando las rutas tecnológicas y las estructuras industriales a una velocidad sin precedentes. La sesión especial "La Nueva Década de la Potencia de Cálculo en IA", celebrada el día 13, se centró en la potencia de cálculo, núcleo fundamental de los sistemas inteligentes, abordando sistemáticamente desde la evolución de la arquitectura y la construcción del ecosistema hasta su implementación industrial.

Author: Zhou Lei, Zhao Zhiqi, Zhang Jiamin  Editor: Zhou Lei  
December 12, 2025, Nanshan, Shenzhen.  
The main forum of the 8th GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Conference officially commenced at 9:30 a.m. at the Sheraton Shenzhen Nanshan Hotel. The two-day conference is jointly organized by the GAIR Institute and Leiphone, with Academician Gao Wen serving as the chair of the steering committee, and Academician Yang Qiang and Professor Zhu Xiaorui as conference chairs.  

As a flagship AI event in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, GAIR has consistently upheld the dual themes of "heritage" and "innovation" since its inception in 2016. From the intellectual legacy of academic luminaries to the ideological continuity among chairs of top Chinese conferences, and the emergence of young scholars, GAIR serves not only as a platform for technical exchange but also as a spiritual home encapsulating four decades of China's AI development.  

After four years, GAIR returns to its home ground in Shenzhen. Over these four years, large-scale models have surged, AI has ascended to greater heights, knowledge production has expanded beyond traditional pathways, and industrial transformation has accelerated. At this year-end juncture, GAIR fulfills its promise, offering high-quality intellectual exchanges to review the rapid pace of technological advancement and present cutting-edge insights into the AI era for the industry and the public.

excerpt_i18n.en: On Saturday at the base of Noitom Robotics, with sunlight spilling onto the ground, we met Dr. Dai Ruoli—co-founder of Noitom, who now also holds the title of founder/CEO of Noitom Robotics. He combines technical acumen with entrepreneurial boldness. Recalling the origins of Noitom over a decade ago, Dr. Dai can still effortlessly recall the product code of the first gyroscope chip in the iPhone—L3G4200D. It was this tiny chip that alerted him to an opportunity, leading to the founding of Noitom. From film visual effects to VR interaction and digital healthcare, Noitom has left its mark across multiple fields. And when the wave of robotics surged, he keenly recognized the potential of robot data. "In 2024, revenue from robotics grew fivefold for Noitom, and it increased again in 2025, ultimately achieving a 40-fold growth over two years. As a business leader, you simply can’t ignore that!" Dr. Dai said with a smile. So, at the beginning of this year, he decisively decided to spin off the robotics business to establish a robot data company. Speaking of this choice, his tone was resolute: "I am the most suitable person to run a robot data company, and Noitom Robotics is the only company in the industry that truly understands how to handle this data business!" Notably, Dr. Dai attended the data session of the 2025 GAIR Global AI and Robotics Conference, delivering a presentation titled "Using Motion Capture...
excerpt_i18n.es: El sábado, bajo el edificio de Noitom Robotics, con el sol brillando en el suelo, nos encontramos con el Dr. Dai Ruoli, cofundador de Noitom, quien ahora también ostenta el título de fundador y CEO de Noitom Robotics. En él se combina la perspicacia tecnológica con la determinación emprendedora. Al recordar los orígenes de Noitom hace más de una década, Dai Ruoli aún puede mencionar de inmediato el código del primer chip giroscópico del iPhone: L3G4200D. Fue este pequeño chip lo que le hizo percibir una oportunidad y fundar Noitom. Desde efectos especiales cinematográficos, hasta interacción en realidad virtual y medicina digitalizada, la huella de Noitom se extiende por diversos campos.
